text:
Zara (PM): Quick design sanity check for a compact review flow for prompt-sets/evals. Goal: make quick triage <30s/test. Main asks: 1) compact scorecard peek inline 2) per-row quick comments 3) a lightweight mobile-friendly approve gesture. Mock: https://figma.com/compact-review-v3
Eli (Design): I like it. Two UX constraints: keep row height readable on desktop but adapt to single-line + chevron on mobile. Proposal: compact peek shows score + tiny delta chip + 3-dot menu for actions. Mobile: swipe-right => approve, swipe-left => request changes (with confirm).
Tara (Frontend): Swipe gestures add complexity but doable with our list virtualization. We'll need to debounce gestures and require a confirm for bulk swipe (avoid accidental mass actions). Also recommend a small preview animation for expand to reduce perceived jank.
Marco (A11y): Accessibility: swipes must have keyboard equivalents and not be the only way to approve. Provide accessible toggles in the 3-dot menu and keyboard shortcuts (a = approve, r = request changes). For colorblind users, delta chips must include text like "+1.2%"/"-0.8%" and an icon (up/down caret). Also request an optional high-contrast scorecard mode in Preferences.
Ben (QA): For bulk actions, require blocking if any selected test has regression > 1.5% or is flagged flaky. If override is allowed, require a comment. Also add a moderation audit entry for all bulk approves with before/after snapshots.
Zara (PM): Copy suggestions: primary = "Approve selection"; override modal = "Approve with override" with required reason; per-row action = "Quick comment" / "Mark flaky" / "Open full scorecard". Keep microcopy terse.
Eli (Design): I'll add a tiny inline comment pill that expands a thread for that test (like a compact chat). Keeps reviewers from opening full detail just to jot a note. Also adding a compact legend for colors/icons in the header.
Tara (Frontend): API needs: 1) GET /runs/:id/summary (per-test delta, flaky flag, short_excerpt, long_output_flag) 2) POST /runs/:id/actions bulk approve/override with optional reason 3) POST /runs/:id/tests/:test_id/comments for quick comments. ETA: proto endpoints in ~3 days. Frontend prototype in ~6 days if we reuse existing components.
Marco (A11y): Additional a11y asks: 1) ensure each row is focusable and exposes aria-expanded when preview opened; 2) announce via aria-live when a bulk action completes ("5 tests approved"); 3) ensure swipe affordance isn't required for keyboard users. I'll draft a checklist for the PR.
Ben (QA): Edge cases: 1) tests updated since reviewer opened list -> show "changed" banner and gray-out auto-approve; 2) long outputs containing markdown/html -> sanitize and render safe preview; 3) concurrent approvals -> surface conflict banner with keep/merge choices.
Zara (PM): Nice. Also want a temporary "compact-mode" toggle so power reviewers can opt-in. Default remains expanded for first-time users. We'll add telemetry event: compact_mode_toggled.
Eli (Design): For colorblind/high-contrast mode, I'll provide alternate palettes and iconography. Also will design a small "delta drilldown" flyout on hover that shows baseline/candidate numbers and metric rule that failed.
Tara (Frontend): Implementation details: virtualized list + lazy-render full diff on expand, optimistic UI for approve with 10s undo, and keep a small client cache for run summary that expires after 20s to reduce API churn. For mobile swipes we'll require >40% swipe threshold to trigger action.
Marco (A11y): Keyboard shortcuts proposed: j/k navigate, Enter expand, a approve, r request changes, c quick-comment, u undo last bulk. Ensure shortcuts are disabled when focus is in an input. Add tests with NVDA/VoiceOver.
Ben (QA): We'll add automated tests for bulk undo, override modal reasons required, and concurrency conflicts. Also add an accessibility regression test for the high-contrast mode.
preview-bot: preview deployed -> https://preview.redwood.ai/runs/1939999999/compact-review; branch -> github.com/redwood/repo/pull/722
Zara (PM): Plan: Eli + Tara to build prototype for demo next Wed, Marco to produce a11y checklist, Ben to author QA matrix, I'll update the RFC and ship a small opt-in experiment. Thanks team! :sparkles:
